outcome: maternal morbidity (blood loss, hospital stay, costs, antibiotic use, catheterization, wound erythema)
neonatal outcomes (umbilical artery pH, NICU admission)
cohort: The study included 114 singleton, term pregnancies with vertex presentation experiencing prolonged deceleration in the second stage of labor.
finding: Cesarean section was associated with increased maternal morbidity compared to instrumental delivery groups, while short-term neonatal outcomes were comparable across all three delivery methods.
mod_finding: Cesarean section led to significantly increased maternal morbidity compared to instrumental delivery methods, but neonatal outcomes were similar regardless of the mode of delivery during prolonged deceleration in the second stage of labor.
